Q: How to switch back from the payment app back to my app? A:

This can happen if the payment screen is opened as a separate activity. After the transaction finishes, Android may keep that activity on top, so your app doesn’t automatically return to the foreground. Instead of navigating to a fragment inside Collect, try bringing your main activity back explicitly when you receive the result. You can start your activity again with flags such as

Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_REORDER_TO_FRONT or Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_SINGLE_TOP.

This usually brings the existing activity to the front instead of creating a new one. It’s also worth checking the NEXO/Besteron documentation to see if they provide a callback or return intent after the transaction. Many payment SDKs expect you to handle that event to bring the app back to the foreground rather than doing the navigation manually.

Q: Strings in C# has 2,147,483,647 characters as maximum? A:

Creating a software system that is truly "0-N scalable" would be very difficult to do while maintaining performance, since you essentially need a virtual machine that uses "bigint" for all addresses and other numbers. You talk about "machine resources", but with virtualization there are no real fixed limits.

There are some limits in .Net due to the requirement to support 32 bit systems. Now that 64-bit systems are ubiquitous it would be useful to support longer buffers, and that would require long or nint for lengths. But this is difficult to change without causing major backward compatibility issues. And there are not that many use cases that would benefit.

But this is more of an issue with things like byte-arrays. The immutable nature of .Net strings make excessively large strings somewhat impractical.

Q: How the firestore support custom class and also custom class support FieldValue with typescript? A:

I found a GitHub discussion about a proposal request for Firestore that somewhat relates to what you're trying to achieve. It seems that the Firestore developers are still looking into adding type support for FieldValue within FirestoreDataConverter. As of now, there's been no indication in the release notes that this has been implemented.

We're also looking into adding type support for FieldValue inside FirestoreDataConverter and type-safe update() calls with some of the new features in Typescript 4.1. Although these changes won't allow you to do everything in a single pass, it'll make adding custom classes in FieldValue and update() easier.

Q: How to filter a length-indexed list (GADT) A:

Unfortunately the AI tools are not wrong that "additional type machinery would be required". The type

filterVec :: (a -> Bool) -> Vec a n -> Vec a m

doesn't cut it – what it expresses is that when calling the function, you get to choose m and it would then somehow magick the result to have that specific length.

Instead, what we would need is an existentially quantified result over m, meaning that when you call the function you have no control over what its value would be.

Haskell has for a long time had various ways of expressing existential types. Nowadays the main approach is with GADTs, but this requires making a clunky separate definition. There is unfortunately still no ∃ quantifier.

A quick (kind of...) and dirty alternative, that's kind of existential without actually using any specific tooling, is to wrap the result into continuation passing style and then use universal quantification on the contravariant part.

filterVec :: ∀ n a r . (a -> Bool) -> Vec a n -> (∀ m . Vec a m -> r) -> r

Q: Running SpringBoot 3 application with Security Configuration A:

The issue is in your model class. In spring boot 3x versions strictly checks within the data types when you run query. Please recheck the model class and your query bind on it.

For example: in your model class your data type is in 'int'. But when you extract data using query in repo layer you get the field as 'String' or other data type. This is strictly checked in V3x. If you need more details please show the model class and repo interface
